title: PaLM 2 Technical Report
measurement_description: The paper measured two main aspects related to religion: 1) The toxicity probability of documents in the English pre-training data that contained references to religious identity terms. 2) The percentage of toxic language generated by the model in a dialog context in response to prompts containing religious identity terms, evaluated across 16 languages.
findings: In the English pre-training data, documents referencing identities such as 'christians,' 'jewish people,' and 'muslim' showed a higher-than-average toxicity probability. In evaluations of generated text, prompts referencing 'Judaism' and 'Islam' produced significantly more toxic responses in English, German, and Portuguese compared to other religious groups and the baseline.
references: Abid, A., Farooqi, M., and Zou, J. Persistent anti-muslim bias in large language models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2101.05783, 2021. URL https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.05783.
